messages:
irina: Quick question — we're updating audit-log retention and immutability rules and I want to call out a few edge cases before the config lands in prod. TL;DR: does KMS key rotation / rollback affect our WORM guarantees for already-archived audit objects and how should we expose proof to customers?

samir: context? is this hosted vs private parity or a single-scheme change?

irina: both. hosted needs to maintain customer-facing verifiable proofs; private (VPC/on-prem) might have different KMS tooling. We want the same end-user guarantee: once an audit event is sealed and included in archive, it must be reproducibly verifiable later even after key rotations.

maria: important callout — rotation shouldn't invalidate previously-produced HMACs/hashes if we store a signing key history or a proof-of-commitment. but if we rely on KMS-encrypt-only without exporting a verification artifact we'll be stuck.

jonathan: concrete options: 1) store an immutable event hash (sha256) and a KMS-encrypted blob containing the event key + metadata; 2) use a detached signature from a signing key stored in KMS with rotation/AUDIT trail; 3) export a signed manifest at daily boundaries and publish anchor to an external transparency log.

irina: leaning toward #1 + daily manifest anchor. questions: how to handle rollback (customer requests key revert), and multipart uploads where parts finish across retention state transitions?

samir: for rollback — we should never allow old keys to be reintroduced as the active signer without rotation markers. if a customer asks to rollback, we need to create a new rotation entry that references the old key ID but signs a new proof. never reuse private key material.

maria: multipart uploads: ensure we finalize and write the sha256 of the assembled object as the canonical artifact, and seal the manifest only after the assemble/complete event. if a part fails and is retried, the final hash will reflect the true stored object.

elaine: also: legal-hold path. If a customer places a hold mid-upload, we must ensure their hold extends object TTL and that immutability flag is set before the manifest signing job runs. failing that, we need a manual flag to reindex and re-sign.

irina: good, add this to the rollout checklist. another concern: schema migrations — we plan an audit event schema v2 (added fields + normalization). how do customers validate exported events across schema versions?

jonathan: include a version field in every event + provide a small compatibility shim in the export tool. also publish a canonical JSON Schema and a change log with examples. customers can run a verify tool that compares stored hash to reserializing via canonical form.

maria: recommend canonicalization algorithm: sort keys, stable float formatting, utf8 normalization. include schema_version and event_type as top-level keys so canonicalization is deterministic.

irina: perfect. now the customer-facing validation API: they can request proof for a time range and we'll return: manifest (signed), list of event hashes, per-event metadata (id, timestamp, schema_version), and verification instructions. ok to include KMS key id references but not raw keys obviously.

samir: agree. also add a signed timeline: manifest payload -> root hash -> signature metadata (kms_key_id, rotation_index). that way we can show which key signed which manifest.

audit-bot: deploy pipeline: manifest-signer v2 scheduled job will run nightly at 02:00 UTC. Config: S3 bucket ark-audit-archives, prefix=sealed/yyyy-MM-dd, signer-role=arn:aws:iam::redwood:role/manifest-signer, kms_key_alias=alias/audit-manifest.

elaine: vuln triage note — we found CVE-2024-xxxxx in multipart-upload helper lib (dependency in the uploader microservice). patch landed (1.2.3 -> 1.2.4) but need emergency backfill check for any partially-committed archives that could have incorrect integrity metadata.

irina: action items: 1) samir — produce design doc for retention parity + rollback-safe signing model (due EOD Friday). 2) maria — add canonicalization & schema migration guidelines to export tool and publish JSON Schema (due Wed). 3) jonathan — add manifest signing metadata fields to customer-facing proof API and include rotation_index (due Thurs). 4) elaine — run backfill scanner for multipart edge cases and report any archives with mismatched computed hash vs stored hash (due ASAP).

samir: noted. one more edge-case: what if a customer rotates their external KMS (private deployment) and we can't access previous signing metadata? for private/on-prem, require customer to provide a public verification key or export of key history during onboarding. document as a mandatory step for Private.

maria: also add retention-proof SLA language: we can provide cryptographic proof for X years; after that proof may require key custody from the customer for private deployments. put suggested wording in the contracts PR.

irina: thanks. I'll open the PR with checklist + link to design doc when samir's draft is ready. keep replies in-thread for traceability. :thumbsup:

jonathan: linking a sketch of the manifest format:```
{
  "manifest_version": "1",
  "date": "2026-03-18",
  "root_hash": "sha256:...",
  "signed_by": { "kms_key_id": "arn:aws:kms:...", "rotation_index": "3" },
  "entries": [ { "event_id": "e-123", "hash": "sha256:...", "schema_version": "2" }, ... ]
}
```

elaine: ack — starting scanner now, will ping here with counts.

maria: small UX ask — export verify-tool should return a single boolean + detailed failure reasons; makes it easier for customers to automate.

irina: agree. thanks everyone. I'll capture minutes and send thread to compliance for review.

audit-bot: incident-tracker created: #INC-2026-042, owner=elaine, severity=low, linked-prs=[internal/manifest-signer#89]
